# No exception — parser returns _LeapSecondDatetime with .second=0
# instead of .second=60. is_leap_second() is the only introspection.
python -c "from htdate_pure import parse, is_leap_second; dt=parse('Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:60 GMT'); print(dt.second, is_leap_second(dt))"
# -> 0 True
description: _LeapSecondDatetime inherits from datetime; .second reads as the post-rollover 0, not the literal 60. Callers checking dt.second == 60 will never see the leap-second flag. README documents is_leap_second() as the right API, but the class doesn't expose a .second==60 shortcut, and __repr__ hides the semantic. Fix is documentation only (or override .second — at risk of breaking datetime invariants).
